title: Helmsman: Strategy & Risk Check-in
summary: Quarterly leadership all-hands focused on strategic priorities for the next 90 days, upcoming product betas, capacity and incident-readiness, hiring cadence, and a brief town-hall style Q&A. Risk topics highlighted: Private deployment timeline, SOC2 gap remediation, and burst capacity for model variants.
transcript:
Header: 2025-03-11 10:00 AM PST | Duration: 58 minutes | Host: Maya Chen | Location: Zoom all-hands

[00:00] Maya Chen: Good morning, everyone, welcome to our Helmsman all-hands. We're gonna move a little briskly, we've got a packed agenda, try to keep questions to the end but ping in Slack if it's urgent. Uh, quick housekeeping, recordings will be posted, notes will go into the #leadership-updates channel.

[00:22] Samir Patel: Quick ops note — infra is stable after last week's patch, we saw the expected regen on some of the older infer nodes, that was a patch to the scheduler, notater — scheduler, my bad, the request router. Latency tail improved by about 6% on average. Small regression in batch packing we addressed.

[01:05] Elena Ruiz: On product, first: beta for streaming function-calls is in private beta, 15 customers on it, looking for more feedback on edge-cases where streaming interleaves with tool calls. Please flag any SDK mismatch. Second: model catalog curation for Q2 — we'll be prioritizing smaller-context 8k variants for hosted to reduce cost.

[02:10] Jordan Lee: Capacity note — Dedicated pools: our target for committed burst headroom is 20% above average peak. We're seeing unpredictable spikes with some customers using long-context reranking; we need better tracking hooks. Also investigating multi-tenant KV cache TTL issues that cause cache thrash when KV keys are evicted quickly. I said KV cash on purpose earlier — sorry — KV cache.

[04:45] Priya Nair: Security update: SOC 2 readiness is progressing but there are two open controls around key rotation automation and quarterly penetration testing. We're engaging a third-party pen test firm next month. On Private deployments, there's an audit ask about HSM integration for customers with FIPS-140 requirements — that's on the roadmap but might shift some timelines.

[07:08] Maya Chen: Quick metrics — MRR growth is on track, usage-driven revenue climbed 9% month-over-month; net retention is stable at 112%. Cost per token improved slightly thanks to batching optimizations. But, we still have pressure on egress cost for embeddings-heavy workloads.

[09:30] Samir Patel: Technical deep-dive summary: the runtime team landed an L2 attention kernel that's giving a 12% perf boost on longer sequences on A100s, but we still need quantization profiles for the new 4-bit path. If your team depends on quantized backends, coordinate with infra so we can run perf matrices.

[12:50] Elena Ruiz: Roadmap specifics — next 90 days focus: 1) shipping private control plane alpha for two customers, 2) Redwood Optimize v1 with basic batching heuristics, 3) rollout of observability traces per request. We are deprioritizing the large-context 512k experiment until we stabilize costs.

[15:01] Audience question (Slack): "What's the timeline for full private on-prem?"

[15:22] Maya Chen: We're aiming for alpha in 6 weeks for the control plane with restricted features. Full on-prem packaged release is likely 4-6 months depending on compliance sign-off. The key gating items are KMS/HSM integrations, install/runbook, and a hardened upgrade path.

[17:40] Jordan Lee: Ops action: we'll be running a dry-run for private upgrade next week in staging; volunteers from eng infra please sign up. Expect a short maintenance window during the dry-run, we'll post details.

[19:05] Audience question: "How are we handling fallbacks when hosted capacity is exhausted?"

[19:22] Samir Patel: We have smart routing policies — automated fallback to cheaper variants or regional routing — but the rollout of fallback SLOs into customer-facing controls is still pending. We're tracking two main failure modes: capacity saturation and KV cache mismatches that lead to latency spikes.

[21:55] Maya Chen: Hiring — we are greenlighted for 25 external hires over the next quarter, priority for runtime engineers, infra SREs, and two security engineers. Internal mobility is encouraged, some roles will be remote-first.

[24:10] Priya Nair: Compliance note again: for enterprise customers we're adding audit log retention options and more granular RBAC. That will affect cost/revenue packaging, so finance/product will align on pricing adjustments.

[26:30] Elena Ruiz: Product experiment: A/B test for batching defaults — we want to see cost delta vs. latency for one of our mid-size customers. If you want to propose a test, submit a short doc to the product experiments board by Friday.

[28:12] Audience: "Clarify the Dedicated SLA — latency targets?"

[28:30] Jordan Lee: Dedicated SLA target is p99 < 450ms for common gen workloads under committed throughput; for heavy reranking workloads we have separate throughput-backed SLOs. The contract templates will be updated in the next release.

[30:40] Maya Chen: Risk log highlight — there are two medium risks: 1) Private deployment delays due to third-party pen test scheduling, 2) Unexpected model licensing constraints for a curated open model we're planning to promote. Both are being tracked on the risk board.

[33:05] Samir Patel: Engineering retrospective — we pushed an infra fix that inadvertently increased cold-starts for small pods; cause was a miswired readiness probe. Fix is in canary, monitoring for regressions.

[35:50] Audience: "Any change to partner strategy?"

[36:02] Maya Chen: Partner strategy is more selective — focusing on cloud-marketplace integrations and a few channel partners in APAC. We will not expand to broad reseller agreements this quarter.

[37:40] Open Q&A rapid-fire — questions pulled from chat.

[37:45] Employee (Speaker 1): On-boarding windows for dedicated customers have been slow, anything planned?

[37:55] Jordan Lee: Yes, dedicated onboarding is getting a new runbook and a dedicated EngOps coordinator to reduce handoffs. Expected to drop onboarding time by ~30%.

[39:30] Employee: Will there be more transparency into per-route cost?

[39:40] Elena Ruiz: Yes, console roadmap includes per-route token cost and a new cost-explorer in Redwood Console in Q2. Early access will be given to power users.

[41:20] Maya Chen: Ok, final thoughts — focus on execution, keep cross-team comms tight. We're in a resilient position but there's no time for complacency.

[41:45] Action recap and next steps readout by Maya.

[42:00] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Private alpha in 6 weeks (Samir + Priya) 2) Pen test engagement next month (Priya) 3) Dry-run upgrade volunteers for staging (Jordan) 4) Product experiment proposals due Friday (Elena) 5) Hiring slate confirmed (People Ops)

[43:20] Meeting ends, chat remains open for follow-up.

Note: transcript contains a few automated transcription artifacts and speaker label noise.
